title: HW telemetry-driven kernel selection and prefill prioritization for mixed MIG fleets
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Reduce 99th-percentile prefill+decode latency on mixed H100/L40S/A10 fleets by using fine-grained hardware telemetry to drive kernel selection and prefill prioritization. We will build a lightweight inference-time scoring layer that picks kernel variants and prefill scheduling priorities based on live signals (MIG slice size, SM utilization, L2 hit rate, memory bandwidth pressure, temperature/clock headroom, KV-cache pressure). The approach avoids blanket heuristics and replaces static SKU maps with empirical, per-workload profiles.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Implement telemetry ingest and per-request scoring that outputs: recommended_kernel_variant, prefill_priority (high/normal/low), and reason_code string

2) Automated experiments on dedicated test fleet show >=15% reduction in 99th-percentile end-to-end prefill+decode latency for chat-style workloads (avg seq_len 512) on mixed MIG configurations without increasing median latency by >5%
3) No regression on throughput P50 or cost-per-token beyond 3% for production traffic in shadow testing
4) Rollout plan (canary -> region -> global) and automatic fallback to conservative kernel map if telemetry feed degrades
5) Dashboard panels added to Console for per-kernel selection frequency, telemetry correlation charts, and rollback triggers
notes: Initial hypothesis: choosing a kernel variant with lower peak SM occupancy but better memory behavior reduces tail lat when memory BW is the bottleneck (observed on smaller MIG slices on H100)
We need to extend runtime telemetry schema to include derived signals: sm_occupancy_pct, avg_warp_util, l2_hit_rate, mem_bw_util_pct, kv_cache_fill_ratio, hw_clock_headroom_pct
Design decision: scoring layer lives in serving-runtime process (fast path ~50-200ns), configuration table versioned via config-store and canaryed independently
Experiment plan split into three phases: local microbench harness -> test fleet A/B -> production shadow
We will prefer kernel variants that lower decode tail even if they produce slightly lower aggregate throughput for latency-sensitive routes (chat/interactive)
Risk: NVIDIA driver/firmware variance across L40S/H100/A10 may produce noise in signals; add smoothing window and minimum sample counts before switching kernels
benchmark_plan: Create microbench job that replays production prompt distribution (seq lengths 64/256/512/1024) across target MIG slice configs (1g.5gb, 2g, full GPU) on H100 and L40S
Measure per-variant metrics: tokens/s, p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, gpu_power_w, sm_occupancy, l2_hit_rate, mem_bw_util, clock_mhz over time
Run each candidate kernel selection policy for at least 30 minutes per config to collect stable tails
Use statistical significance test (bootstrap) for p99 comparison and record effect size
implementation_tasks: Telemetry: add derived signals and sample rate controls (ENG-telemetry module)
Scoring service: lightweight policy evaluator in runtime with hot-config override
Kernel selector: bridge from score -> kernel table; support hysteresis counters to avoid thrashing
Prefill scheduler: implement multi-queue prefill priorities and priority aging
Experiment infra: A/B toggles, shadow run pipeline, automatic metrics export to DataDog and Console
Rollback: implement conservative kernel map and circuit-breaker when telemetry stalls
